WEST PAKISTAN ORDINANCE NO. XX OF 1969
AN
ORDINANCE
to fix the minimum rates of wages
for unskilled workers employed in certain commercial and industrial
establishments in West Pakistan.
1. Short title, extent, commencement and applications.‑----
(1) This Ordinance may be called the Omitted words "West Pakistan". ibid. s. 3(a).
* * * Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers Ordinance, 1969.
(2) It extends to the whole of Subs. for "the Province of West Pakistan. except the
Tribal Area" by P.O. 4 of 1975, s. 2 (1) & Sch.[Pakistan] Ordinance applied to the Tribal areas of Baluchistan by
Regulation III of 1974 (29 July 1974), Baluchistan Gaz, Extr. 29th July 1974.
(3) It shall be deemed to have come into force on and from the
first day of July, 1969.
(4) It shall apply to every commercial and industrial
establishment Omitted words "wherein fifty or more
persons arc employed or were employed on any day during the preceding twelve
months." by the West Pakistan Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers
(Amendment) Ordinance, 2001 (LVII of 2001), s. 3(b), (effective retrospectively
from August 1, 2001); Gaz. of Pak., Extra. Pt.1. Oct, 22, 2001, p. 1515‑1516.
* * * * * but shall not apply to‑‑
(a) persons in the service of Pakistan, as
defined in Subs. for "Article 242 of the
constitution of 1962" by P.O 4 of 1975, s.2 (1) & Sch.[Article
260 of the Constitution],
(b) any establishment, undertaking or
installation relating to the Defence Services, civil armed forces, postal,
telegraph and telephone services, ports, railways, fire‑fighting
services, electricity, gas, water‑supply, public conservancy and
hospitals; and
(c) any establishment or undertaking, which
Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, declares to be engaged in
a public utility service for the purposes of this Ordinance.
COMMENTARY
Before the October 2001 amendment
in above sub‑section (4), the 1969 Ordinance was applicable to every
industrial and commercial establishment "wherein fifty or more persons are
employed or were employed on any day during the preceding twelve months."
With the omission of applicability condition of "fifty or more
persons", the Ordinance is now applicable to all establishments regardless
of the number of‑workers‑(even one person) is employed.

AN
ORDINANCE
to fix the minimum rates of wages
for unskilled workers employed in certain commercial and industrial
establishments in West Pakistan.
2. Definitions.
In this Ordinance, unless the
context otherwise requires‑
(a) "apprentice" means a learner
who is paid an allowance during the period of training;
(b) "commercial establishment"
means an establishment in which the business of advertising, commission or
forwarding is conducted or which is a commercial agency and includes a clerical
department of a factory or of any industrial or commercial undertaking, the
office establishment of a person who for the purpose of fulfilling a contract
with the owner of any commercial establishment or industrial establishment,
employs workmen, a unit of a joint‑stock company, an insurance company, a
banking company or a bank, a broker's office or stock exchange, a club, a
hotel, a restaurant or an eating house, a cinema or theatre, and such other
establishment or class thereof, as government may, by notification in the
official Gazette, declare to be commercial establishment for the purposes of
this Ordinance;
(c) "employer"
means a person owing or having charge of the business of a commercial or
industrial establishment and includes an agent or manager or any other person
acting on behalf of such person in the general management or control of such
establishment;
(d) "Government"
means the Subs. for "Government of West
Pakistan" by P.O 4 of 1975, s.2 (1) & Sch.[Provincial
Government;]
(e) "industrial
area" means the districts of Hyderabad, Lyallpur, Lahore, Multan and
Sheikhupura and Kotri Taluka in Dadu District, and any other area which
Government may, by notification in the Official wit Gazette, declare to be an
Industrial Area for the purposes of this Ordinance:
(f) "industrial establishment"
means‑
(i) a mine or quarry;
(ii) a workshop or other establishment in
which the work of making, altering, repairing, ornamenting, finishing or
packing or otherwise treating any article or substance with a view to its use,
sale, transport, delivery, or disposal is carried on, or where any such service
is rendered to a customer; and
(iii) any other establishment which Government
may, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare to be an industrial
establishment;
(g) "wages"
means all cash remuneration payable to a workman, and includes dearness
allowance, house rent, conveyance allowance, Words
inserted by the West Pakistan Minimum
Wages for Unskilled Workers (Amendment) Act, 1993 (IX of 1993), (effective from
July 1. 1992); Gaz. of Pak., Extr, Pt. I, p. 105. April 10, 1993. [cost
of living allowance, special allowances] and any other fixed allowance, but
does not include travelling allowance, gratuity or bonus.
(h) "unskilled
worker" means a worker employed to do unskilled labour; and
(i) "worker"
means any person employed in a commercial or industrial establishment.

WEST PAKISTAN ORDINANCE NO. XX OF 1969
AN
ORDINANCE
to fix the minimum rates of wages
for unskilled workers employed in certain commercial and industrial
establishments in West Pakistan.
3. Minimum wages in commercial and industrial establishments.‑--
Every unskilled worker, other
than an apprentice employed in a commercial or industrial establishment
situated in an area specified in column I of the Schedule, shall be paid wages
at a rate not lower than the minimum wages per month specified against such
area in column 2 of the Schedule:
Provided that where an employer
provides housing accommodation to a worker, he may deduct from the wages of
such a worker. an amount not exceeding that specified in column 3 of the
Schedule, and where the employer provides a worker with transport to and from
the place of work, he may deduct from the wages of such a worker an amount not
exceeding that specified in column 4 of the Schedule.
Subs.

means a normal working period of twenty‑six days calculated at the rate
of forty‑eight hours of work per week; and

COMMENTARY
The minimum wage was increased
from Rs. 1500 to Rs. 2500 pin (in col. 2 of Schedule) for unskilled workers.
Every employer is responsible to pay that amount regardless of the number of
workers in his establishment. In this new basic wage in which all previous
Federal and Provincial cost of living allowances, dearness and special
allowances are merged which were announced from time to time since August 1993
under the Employees Cost of Living (Relief/ Act, 1973 ‑‑ totaled
Rs. 550 per month (Rs. 650 per month for Sindh). All previous COLA
NOTIFICATIONS since August 1993, due to merging, effectively became null and
void. Any new COLAs or allowances announced through notification in future by
either the Federal and Provincial Governments will be added on top of this
basic wage.
Retrospective application of the law:
The courts gave the following
judgements on the question of retrospective application of the law in an appeal
to Supreme Court where an employer challenged the provisions (section 3) of
West Pakistan Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers (Amendment/ Act, 1993 (XI of
1993), promulgated on April 10, 1993 but made effective from July 1, 1992,
which increased minimum wages from Rs. 140 to Rs. 1500 pin for unskilled
workers. Again, West Pakistan Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers !Amendment)
Ordinance, 2001 (LVII of 2001), promulgated on October 22, 2001 but made
effective retrospectively from August 1, 2001, increased minimum wages from Rs.
1500 to Rs. 2500 pin for unskilled workers.

Gaz. of West Pakistan, Extra., September 1, 1969, p. 1399.
[28th August
1969]
WEST PAKISTAN ORDINANCE NO. XX OF 1969
AN
ORDINANCE
to fix the minimum rates of wages
for unskilled workers employed in certain commercial and industrial
establishments in West Pakistan.
4. Responsibility for payment of minimum wages.
(1) Every employer shall be
responsible for the payment of minimum wages required to be paid under this
Ordinance to all unskilled workers employed, either directly or through a
contractor, in his commercial or industrial establishment.
(2) Where an unskilled worker
employed in a commercial industrial establishment to which this Ordinance
applies has been paid wages for tile mouth of July, 1969, at a rate less than
the minimum rate of wages to which he is entitled under this Ordinance, the
employer shall, within thirty days of the promulgation of this Ordinance, pay
such worker the difference between the amount actually paid to him and the
amount he is entitled under this Ordinance.

5. Agreements under duress to be void.
All agreements arrived at between
the employers and the workers under duress at any time during the period from
the 1st day of March. 1969 to the 25th day of March, 1969, shall, with effect
from the date‑of coming into force of this Ordinance, be void.
Explanation.‑‑--- In this section the words "under
duress" include circumstances in which due to fear either party is in a
state of mental incompetence to resist pressure improperly brought to bear due
to violence, or threat of violence.

6. Effect of laws, orders, agreements etc., inconsistent with this
Ordinance.‑‑--
The provisions of this Ordinance
shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in
any other law or in any order or notification made or issued under any such law
or in any award, agreement or contract of service:
Provided that where under any
such law, order, notification, award agreement or contract of service, other
than an agreement declared to be void under section 5, an unskilled worker is
entitled to wages which are higher than the minimum wages required to he paid
under this Ordinance, he shall continue to be paid such higher wages.

any offence under this ordinance save on a complaint made by an aggrieved worker
